newsitem.title: EGYPT: Women survive Cairo apartment block collapse.
newsitem.headline: Women survive Cairo apartment block collapse.

text.p: Egyptian rescue workers on Tuesday found two women - one American and one Egyptian - alive after 36 hours under the rubble of a collapsed Cairo apartment building where they had gone to look at a flat, a friend said.

Samantha Miksche, 22, a U.S. citizen, was looking at the flat in the Cairo suburb Heliopolis on Sunday with her mother, a friend and two relatives. Half-an-hour after they arrived, the 11-storey building caved in on them and at least 100 others.

"She was visiting her mom's relatives and they wanted a place to rent. Unfortunately they were looking at the flat when it (the building) fell down," Noha Wagih told Reuters by telephone by the woman's bedside.
Miksche and friend Noha Fawzi were pulled out alive on Tuesday suffering from abrasions but Miksche's mother and relatives are still buried, along with at least 90 others.

Distraught relatives were losing hope on Tuesday that they would see their loved ones emerge alive from under the mountain of concrete and twisted steel reinforcements that was once the 11-storey residential block.
The Interior Ministry has said prosecutors were questioning the owner of the building, Raouf Wissa Ibrahim, for illegally adding five storeys after getting permission to build one.
Soaring Cairo real estate prices have often pushed landlords to add extra floors to their properties illegally.
Several buildings have collapsed beneath the extra weight and recent earthquakes have also taken their toll on poorly constructed buildings in the crowded capital.
